Ivan IV, called the Terrible, was grand prince of Moscow from 1533 and, from 1547, the first ruler crowned tsar of all Russia. He ruled until his death in 1584, and his reign made the Tsardom of Russia an empire of many peoples.

  • He took the Khanate of Kazan in 1552 and the Astrakhan Khanate in 1556, giving Russia the whole Volga down to the Caspian. Peoples such as the Mari came under Russian rule. Saint Basil's Cathedral in Moscow marks the taking of Kazan.
  • He welcomed the English captain Richard Chancellor in 1553, which led to the Muscovy Company and English trade through the White Sea.
  • He fought the long Livonian War from 1558 to 1583 for a Baltic coast, and lost.
  • Late in his reign the Stroganov merchants sent the Cossack Yermak across the Urals, the start of the conquest of Siberia.

His early years brought reforms, a new law code in 1550 and the first assembly of the land. After his wife Anastasia died in 1560 he grew suspicious and cruel. In 1565 he set up the oprichnina, a private realm whose black-clad horsemen terrorised the nobles, and in 1570 they massacred the people of Novgorod. In 1581 he struck and killed his own son and heir in a rage. His weak son Feodor died childless in 1598, ending the dynasty and opening the Time of Troubles.
sum: Ivan IV, called the Terrible, was grand prince of Moscow from 1533 and, from 1547, the first ruler crowned tsar of all Russia. He ruled until his death in 1584, and his reign made the Tsardom of Russia an empire of many peoples.
